Goal - examine combinations of several characteristics within the same patients
and see if particular combinations have impact on deaths

Library
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(broom)
```

Load clean data
```{r}
clean_data <- read_tsv(file = "data/03_dat_aug.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```


Patients are divided into categories based on smoking exposure, lung function,
and CHF (congestive heart failure) status
```{r}
profile_data <- clean_data |>
  mutate(
    smoking_group = if_else(
      packyrs > 0,
      "Smoking exposure",
      "No smoking exposure"
    ),

    lung_group = if_else(
      fev < median(fev, na.rm = TRUE),
      "Lower FEV",
      "Higher FEV"
    ),

    chf_group = if_else(
      chf == 1,
      "CHF",
      "No CHF"
    )
  )
```


As we see that smoking alone is not statistically significant cause of death
but patients who smoke still experience high death rates it could cause death in combination with other factors.
Is smoking exposure associated with higher mortality particularly among patients
with lower FEV?

```{r}
deceased_lung <- profile_data |>
  filter(death == 1) |>
  count(
    smoking_group,
    lung_group,
    name = "deceased_patients"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(deceased_patients))

View(deceased_lung)
```


Calculating mortality proportions for smoking and lung function

```{r}
mortality_lung <- profile_data |>
  group_by(smoking_group, lung_group) |>
  summarise(
    patients = n(),
    deaths = sum(death == 1),
    mortality_rate = mean(death == 1) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mortality_rate))

View(mortality_lung)
```


Visualize mortality by smoking exposure and lung function
```{r}
lung_plot <- mortality_lung |>
  mutate(
    profile = paste(
      smoking_group,
      lung_group,
      sep = " + "
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = reorder(profile, mortality_rate),
    y = mortality_rate
  )) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(
      deaths, "/", patients,
      " (", round(mortality_rate, 1), "%)"
    )),
    hjust = -0.1,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.35))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mortality by smoking exposure and lung function",
    x = "Patient characteristics",
    y = "Mortality (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

lung_plot
```

Identify deceased patients by smoking exposure and CHF

```{r}
deceased_chf <- profile_data |>
  filter(death == 1) |>
  count(
    smoking_group,
    chf_group,
    name = "deceased_patients"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(deceased_patients))

View(deceased_chf)
```


Mortality proportions between CHF and smoking:
```{r}
mortality_chf <- profile_data |>
  group_by(smoking_group, chf_group) |>
  summarise(
    patients = n(),
    deaths = sum(death == 1),
    mortality_rate = mean(death == 1) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mortality_rate))

View(mortality_chf)
```


Visualizing mortality proportions:
```{r}
chf_plot <- mortality_chf |>
  mutate(
    profile = paste(

    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = reorder(profile, mortality_rate),

  )) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(
      deaths, "/", patients,
      " (", round(mortality_rate, 1), "%)"
    )),
    hjust = -0.1,
    size = 3.5
  ) +

chf_plot
```

Statistical analysis:
```{r}
profile_data |>
  mutate(
    combination = paste(smoking_group, lung_group, sep = " + ")
  ) |>
  select(combination, death) |>
  table() |>
  chisq.test()
```
Chi-square test did not identify a statistically significant association between the four patient profiles and mortality

```{r}
profile_data |>
  mutate(
    combination = paste(smoking_group, chf_group, sep = " + ")
  ) |>
  select(combination, death) |>
  table() |>
  chisq.test()
```
CHF and smoking combination is statistically significant
